subject: Unexpected prefetch token counts / collection retry
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@rainloop.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected token surge on 2026-08-31 — invoice question

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing a large spike on our August invoice (invoice_202608.pdf attached) that looks like tokens generated by what our SDK calls 'prefetch' or warmup requests. The main window is 2026-08-31 02:00–03:30 UTC — roughly 1.2M extra tokens compared to baseline.

Can your team confirm whether those warmup/prefetch calls are being billed as normal consumption? We have an internal flag that should mark these as non-billable but the telemetry shows the calls hitting your inference endpoint as normal requests.

Attached: usage_snapshot_20260831.csv (sample of request ids / timestamps).

We'd like:
- confirmation whether these requests were counted on your side as billable tokens
- a plan for collection retry / provisional credit if they were mis-attributed
- how any credit would be handled with respect to VAT (RainLoop is EU-registered)

We're happy to provide more logs if you need them. This is blocking our accounts payable team — they put the invoice on hold pending your confirmation.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Finance, RainLoop AI
Elena Martinez | RainLoop AI
elena@rainloop.ai | +44 20 7123 4567

[attachment: usage_snapshot_20260831.csv]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@rainloop.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected token surge on 2026-08-31 — invoice question

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for sending the snapshot. Sorry for the trouble; I'll loop in our billing lead Ben and Kim from account ops to dig in.

Immediate plan:
1) Ben will pull a short window export (server-side) and look for request id patterns / duplicate early responses.
2) If we determine these were client-side warmups being counted, we can propose a provisional credit while we complete the audit.
3) We'll confirm VAT handling once we know whether this is a credit (post-tax adjustment) or a reversal.

Can you confirm the exact invoice number you put on hold (it looks like invoice_202608.pdf but I want to be sure) and whether RainLoop prefers a credit memo or a negative line on next invoice?

I'll re-open once Ben has the initial analysis (should be within 24h).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Billing Ops | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@rainloop.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected token surge on 2026-08-31 — invoice question

Hi Elena — I pulled the server-side logs for the window you called out and compared them to your usage snapshot. Summary of findings:

- There is a dense cluster of requests from RainLoop's API key during 2026-08-31T02:05:12Z to 2026-08-31T03:22:44Z.
- Many requests include the header X-RL-PREFETCH: true and an id pattern pref_XXXX that matches your CSV sample.
- On our runtime these were processed as normal generation requests and counted against tokens; the runtime currently does not automatically filter prefetch markers from billing.

Prelim numbers: ~1.15M tokens attributable to requests flagged prefetch; per your plan I can propose a provisional credit of 60% of that surge while we do a deeper attribution (the percentage accounts for any partial real usage during warmup). That would translate to a provisional credit of $3,420 (estimate) to be applied to your account pending audit.

Collection / invoice handling:
- We will schedule a billing collection retry on 2026-09-05 for the current outstanding amount but mark the invoice as under audit to avoid collection escalation.
- If RainLoop confirms you prefer a credit memo, we'll issue a credit memo referencing invoice_202608.pdf which will reduce the outstanding balance.
- VAT: for EU-registered customers we generally issue credit memos net of VAT and then post VAT adjustments in the next tax cycle. If you prefer a full reversal that includes VAT, please confirm and we'll route to tax.

I've attached a short log excerpt (billing_logs_excerpt.txt) and the invoice PDF snapshot (invoice_202608.pdf). Next steps:
- Can you confirm RainLoop prefers a credit memo (we'll issue it from Redwood) or a negative line on the next invoice?
- Confirm whether the registered VAT id on file is GB999888777 (so we route the credit correctly).

Once you confirm, we'll:
- Apply a provisional credit and note it against the current outstanding balance
- Complete the full audit (expected 3–5 business days) and either finalize the credit or reconcile with additional evidence

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Analyst | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
[attachments: invoice_202608.pdf, billing_logs_excerpt.txt]

From: Elena Martinez <elena@rainloop.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, finance@rainloop.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected token surge on 2026-08-31 — invoice question

Ben / Tessa — thanks for the quick analysis and for the proposed provisional credit. We confirm:

- Invoice on hold: invoice_202608.pdf (confirmed).
- Please issue a credit memo referencing invoice_202608.pdf for the provisional amount you suggested ($3,420) while you complete the audit. We prefer a credit memo rather than a negative line.
- VAT id on file is EU123456789 (we appear to have two VAT ids on our account; please use EU123456789). RainLoop is VAT-registered in NL.
- For tax purposes, please mark the credit memo as 'provisional — subject to audit' and include the billing_logs_excerpt.txt link for our records.

A few asks from our side:
- Will the provisional credit reduce the amount your collection retry attempts on 2026-09-05? (We want to avoid a retry for the full disputed amount.)
- If the audit finds less than the provisional credit should be applied, how will the difference appear on our next statement?

Appreciate the responsiveness — this will let our AR team clear the hold.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Finance, RainLoop AI
elena@rainloop.ai
